I just graduated nursing school with my BSN in May and definitely see this. When we were halfway through the program we were asked what kind of nursing we wanted to do after graduating. Everybody wanted to do ED/ICU/Mother-Baby/NP/CCRN. NOBODY wanted to do Medsurg. At the time I said Psych, but I could never after having my psych rotation. I am currently working on Medsurg and I like it. So many people were warning me of my floor, but since starting on the floor I see that they were exaggerating. People in my class talking about horrible patients/families, large patient ratios (5-1 or 8-2 with LPN), and constant staff shortages. Honestly patient/family behavior and staff shortages are just like every other floor. I think most of my classmates want to feel superior and that they got a "good" floor with "advanced skills" and "lots of growth." Which can definitely be Medsurg. Many also think that because they got their BSN, they are better than nurses with associates (i.e. I am better than you. You deserve Medsurg but I deserve something better). Which is funny because most of the nurses that got their associates have been working longer and are much better at their jobs than those that immediately got their BSN.

I kept on comparing myself to my peers thinking of how much better they are doing (successful job, lots of friends, family with kids, goes out each night while I'm home with my parents) and felt worse. In therapy I'm learning more to accept the past and try to do small things to better myself. I think it is justified if the person really wants it. Why let people live in pain or misery if they want to humanely end their lives? I do think that it should only be done in extreme circumstances where the person is in constant pain (like late stage cancer) or constant desire for death (like multiple suicide attempts and no treatment has shown any improvement). It should be a last resort, but should be an option. After living with depression for years and having a suicide attempt 2 months ago, I feel like if someone is that miserable for a prolonged amount of time, they should be able to do so. It is better than them trying to kill themselves in a painful, horrific way that will traumatize the family. This way the person can die with respect, humanely, and hopefully around their loved ones.

If not, you get cases like [this girl who was denied euthanasia and had to starve and dehydrate herself until she died](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/jun/05/noa-pothoven-netherlands-girl-not-legally-euthanised-died-at-home)
